units.function: CLI tests for creating/listing/revoking Agent API keys and board API keys, including Agent reference resolution, standard scope, TTL-derived expiration and explicit non-expiring board credentials.
units.dependencyDirection: The Vitest suite registers Token Commander commands, stubs fetch/output and uses fake time for TTL calculation. It verifies client payloads and plaintext JSON output but not server token generation, hashing, authorization or use.
units.keyDataModels: Company/Agent/key IDs, Agent key name and standard scope; board key name/requested company/created/last-used/revoked/expires timestamps; one-time plaintext token returned by create.
units.lifecycle: Resolve Agent by id or company-scoped reference; create/list/revoke Agent key; create board key with client-computed expiry or no expiry; list/revoke board keys; print newly issued plaintext credentials.
units.testAssessment: Focused Vitest passed 6/6 tests on 2026-08-19 and CLI no-emit TypeScript passed. It covers reference resolution, standard Agent scope, deterministic TTL calculation and board key lifecycle routing. It omits caller authority, one-time-output safeguards, scope/audience, maximum TTL, clock skew, hashing, entropy, rotation, concurrent revoke/use, audit events, rate limits and actual expiry enforcement.
units.designRationale: Provide simple credentials for external Agent and administrator automation, exposing metadata for lifecycle management and offering expiration as an operator choice.
units.companyOsProblem: Company OS must distinguish real-human sessions, service accounts, Agent/Connector runtime attestations and local execution-node credentials with independent audience, scope, lifetime, revocation and audit semantics across cloud and self-hosted deployments.
units.companyOsFit: REIMPLEMENT the credential model behind IdentityPort/Connector attestation/SecretPort. Retain opaque key IDs, default short TTL, last-used/revoked metadata and one-time issuance, but require audience/resource scopes, issuer/subject, deployment binding, maximum lifetime, rotation and responsible-human authorization. Prefer OIDC/SSO and short-lived exchange over broad static board tokens; prohibit non-expiring privileged tokens by default.
units.responsibilityConflict: A board token collapses all human board actors into one broad automation persona, preventing reliable attribution to the real accountable person. An Agent key is also not sufficient runtime proof: it does not bind a specific Work, Connector version, permission/data contract or result.

2026-08-19 focused Vitest: 1 file and 6 tests passed
securityFindings: Critical design risk: privileged board credentials can be explicitly non-expiring, increasing theft persistence and weakening mandatory rotation/re-certification.
New plaintext Agent and board tokens are serialized to stdout JSON, where terminal capture, shell pipelines, CI logs and caller logging can persist them.
Board-token payload carries requestedCompanyId but no tested audience, role/capability/resource scope, human subject or approval authority.
Agent key scope is only `{kind: standard}` in the test; least-privilege tool/data/Work/deployment restrictions and runtime attestation are absent.
Expiry is calculated client-side from local clock; maximum TTL, clock skew and server-owned policy/enforcement are not tested.
Create/list/revoke calls have no tested step-up authentication, responsible-human approval, idempotency, reason, audit receipt or concurrent-use fencing.
Token entropy, prefix/format validation, secure hashing, constant-time verification, rate limiting and revocation propagation are outside this unit.
